I always have to teak the settings there a bit, the default meat seems to much so I go one above single cut. and the knives not sold at vendors seems silly to me I don't want to break it making them common, but in those time everyone would have a knife so they should not be hard to find especially with all the general stores and weapon smiths that are around. I also love having a cashes from hunterborn where I can hide some of my extra loot early on, or just pile up alchemy ingredients and spare meat, I like to set it to not rot and then put a stash near a river like I'm using the cold water to keep it chilled and make it last.

I set it for realistic meat, and set the meat to rot. That way I have a reason to sell the extra I don't need, so I have a reason to keep hunting. It also forces me to travel light. With meat set to not rot, I found myself just stockpiling food on a companion, and later in my main house/homestead, which kinda defeated the purpose in my mind.

I usually set the knives to be common on vendors, for the same reasons. It's such a required tool, it needs to be everywhere.

I usually use the caches to store arrows, potions, and bandages (from a mod). There's so many of them, and they are needed, but I need to keep light. So, I usually dump a cache in each of the forts when I liberate them, one in each of the smaller villages, one in each of the cities that are too small for a house, since the homesteads are so far out of the way, and one at intersections of major roads, usually at the road sign. That way, I know that no matter where I am, I'm nearby healing items and arrows without having to truck back to one of my houses, giving me a bit of security, and lets me stay out in a field a bit longer. I usually refill them after I finish a dungeon, on my way back to sell loot. Whatever extra potions and arrows I get, I'll dump in to whatever caches are on the way back.
